h1: The 7 Best Budget Printers for a Home Office, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Budget Printers for Home Offices: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 budget home office printers from Canon, HP, Brother and Epson, compared on running cost, scanning, duplex and laser vs inkjet.
summary: The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 is the budget printer to buy if you print every week, because refillable ink bottles cut the two-year running cost far below cartridge machines. The Canon PIXMA TR4720 is the best low-cost all-in-one for scanning multi-page paperwork, and the Brother HL-L2405W is the wireless mono laser for text-heavy offices. The Canon PIXMA TS4320 is the cheapest way into a full-feature inkjet.
intro: The sticker price is the least important number on a budget printer. A machine that costs little on the shelf can cost several times more over two years in cartridges, and that is the trap that catches most home office buyers: they save at checkout and pay for it at every refill. The question to ask is how often you print, and what a page costs when you do.

This ranking sorts seven printers on that basis. We reviewed listings, feature sets and ink systems, and weighed running cost, scan and copy features, duplex printing, wireless setup and support terms against the price bucket. Where a listing does not give a page yield or ink cost, we do not invent one. We judge the type of ink system and let you decide how much you print.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Wireless Color All-in-One Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: A cartridge-free tank printer that delivers the lowest two-year ink cost in the ranking.
products.description:
Epson's ET-2800 swaps cartridges for refillable ink bottles, and still prints, scans and copies in color over Wi-Fi. It lands in the $100 to $200 tier, the top of the budget range.

It wins because ink is where a printer's real cost lives. Refilling a tank from a bottle is far cheaper per page than swapping cartridges, so the higher purchase price is recovered if you print regularly. It is also compact for a tank model. The trade is the up-front cost, which is the highest here, and a cheaper machine can make more sense if you print only a few pages each month.

Buy it if you print weekly or more, or you are tired of cartridge prices. Skip it if you print only occasionally, since ink in a tank can dry out if the printer sits idle for long stretches.
pros: Refillable tanks slash cost per page
Compact for an ink tank model
products.idealFor: Home offices that print every week.
products.skipIf: You print only a few pages a month.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: A low-cost color all-in-one with an auto document feeder for multi-page scanning and copying.
products.description:
Canon built the TR4720 around an auto document feeder, then added wireless, mobile printing and a legacy fax. Color inkjet, $50 to $100.

It ranks second because the document feeder is the feature that separates a real office printer from a basic one. Scanning a ten-page contract without lifting the lid for each sheet saves a lot of time. The fax is a legacy bonus few offices use. Against the EcoTank it is far cheaper to buy, but it uses cartridges, so running costs are higher if you print a lot.

Buy it if you scan and copy more than you print. Skip it if you print every day, where cartridge costs add up.
pros: Auto document feeder for multi-page jobs
products.idealFor: Offices that scan and copy paperwork often.
products.skipIf: You print daily and want cheap ink.

products.name: Brother HL-L2405W Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A compact wireless mono laser that suits text documents and works with Alexa voice commands.
products.description:
Brother's HL-L2405W is a small black-and-white laser that prints over Wi-Fi and from phones, answers to Alexa commands and comes with a Refresh Subscription trial. There is no scanner or copier, and the price tier is $100 to $200.

It ranks third because laser toner suits text-heavy offices. Toner does not dry out the way inkjet ink can, so the printer survives long idle periods, which matters for a home office that prints in bursts. It loses to the EcoTank on features, since it has no scanner, and to the TR4720 on versatility. Check the subscription terms before enrolling, since subscription plans add recurring cost.

Buy it for invoices, contracts and reports. Skip it if you need color or a scanner.
pros: Laser toner will not dry out
products.idealFor: Text-heavy offices that print in bursts.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Duplex color inkjet with a 1.42-inch OLED display that guides you through errors.
products.description:
Look at the control panel first: a 1.42-inch OLED display sits on the TS6520, alongside duplex printing and a built-in copier and scanner. Color inkjet, $50 to $100.

It ranks fourth because the display is a practical edge. Paper jams, low ink and setup prompts show on screen, instead of leaving you hunting for an LED pattern in the manual. Duplex printing halves paper use for double-sided documents. It ranks below the TR4720 because it has no document feeder in its listing, which makes multi-page scanning slower.

Buy it if you value clear on-screen guidance. Skip it if you scan stacks of pages.
pros: OLED display guides you through errors
products.idealFor: Users who want clear on-screen guidance.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A simple-to-set-up all-in-one with a 3-month Instant Ink trial.
products.description:
HP aims the DeskJet 4355 at people unpacking their first office printer: color print, scan and copy, a short wireless setup flow, and a 3-month Instant Ink trial. The $50 to $100 price tier applies, and the listing mentions optional AI-capable printing features.

It ranks fifth because ease of onboarding is its strength, and for a first home office that matters. The tradeoff is Instant Ink: it is a subscription, and subscription plans can lock you into recurring charges and sometimes make the printer depend on the service. Read the terms before you enroll. Against the Canon models it is comparable on features and lacks a document feeder or display to stand out.

Buy it if you want the simplest setup. Skip it if you dislike subscription ink programs.
pros: Prints, scans and copies in color

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A compact duplex color inkjet with scanner and copier at the lowest upfront cost.
products.description:
At the entry of Canon's inkjet range, the TS4320 packs duplex printing, a scanner and copier, mobile app printing and a 1-year limited warranty into a small body. Expect $50 to $100.

It ranks sixth because the other Canon inkjets add either a document feeder or an OLED display, and the TS4320 has neither. It is a single-tray machine, so paper handling is basic. Still, duplex at this price is a good deal for occasional use.

Buy it if you print occasionally and want the lowest outlay. Skip it if you will print a lot, where cartridge costs will exceed the savings.
pros: Duplex printing at a low price
products.idealFor: Occasional printers on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You print weekly and want low ink costs.

products.name: Canon imageCLASS LBP6030w Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A 19 PPM mono laser with wireless, no scanner, no copier and no duplex.
products.description:
Canon rates the LBP6030w at 19 PPM, and it is wireless with a 1-year limited warranty. Scanning, copying and duplex are all absent, and it falls in the $50 to $100 tier.

It ranks last because it does one thing. For a home office that only prints text documents, that can be enough, and the laser approach keeps per-page cost low. But no duplex and no scanner mean extra steps and potentially a second device.

Buy it for plain text printing at the lowest per-page cost. Skip it if you need to scan, copy or print on both sides.
pros: Laser toner does not dry out
products.idealFor: Text-only printing at the lowest cost.
products.skipIf: You need scanning or double-sided output.

whatMatters.detail: Cartridge printers are cheap to buy and costly to feed, while ink tank and laser printers invert that. Estimate your monthly pages and compare. Light users may be fine with a cheap inkjet, and heavy users should look at the EcoTank or a laser.

Laser printers give crisp text and tolerate long idle periods, but the budget models are black and white. Inkjets print color and photos, but ink can dry out if you do not print for weeks. Choose by your mix of documents.
An all-in-one adds a flatbed scanner and copier. An auto document feeder, as on the TR4720, scans multiple pages unattended. If you handle contracts or receipts, check the listing for a feeder.
Automatic duplex prints both sides of a page and saves paper. The TS4320 and TS6520 offer it, while the LBP6030w does not. If you print long documents, it is worth having.
Programs such as Instant Ink and Refresh can lower costs for some users but add recurring charges, and some printers refuse to work without them. Read the terms before enrolling.

faq.q: Are budget printers compatible with my laptop and phone?
faq.a: Most support wireless printing and mobile apps. The Canon models list mobile printing, the Brother adds Alexa support, and the EcoTank is wireless. Check your operating system on the maker's support page before buying.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with cheap printers?
faq.a: Judging by purchase price. Cartridges can cost more over two years than the printer, so a cheap inkjet is a poor buy for heavy use. Match the ink system to how much you print.

faq.q: Is the EcoTank worth it over a $50 to $100 inkjet?
faq.a: If you print every week, yes, because refill bottles are much cheaper per page. If you print a handful of pages a month, a cartridge machine like the TS4320 costs less overall.
Most take about 15 to 30 minutes: install ink, load paper, connect to Wi-Fi through the control panel or app. The HP DeskJet 4355 emphasises a simple setup flow.

faq.q: How do I keep inkjet nozzles from clogging?
faq.a: Print a page now and then, especially in dry climates, and power the printer off from its button. Laser printers like the Brother avoid this problem.

faq.q: Do I need the fax on the TR4720?
faq.a: Almost certainly not. It is a legacy feature that some offices still use. For most home offices, the document feeder is the more useful addition.

finalTake: For a home office that prints often, the Epson EcoTank ET-2800 is the budget printer to buy, because cheap refills outweigh the higher price. The Canon PIXMA TR4720 is the best low-cost all-in-one for scanning paperwork, and the Brother HL-L2405W is the choice for text-only offices. The TS4320 is the minimum-outlay inkjet. Decide how many pages you print, then pick the ink system.
